A Fitted Model

Source: R/statmod.R
StatmodFit-class.Rd

statmod() returns an object of this class. It holds three things: the specification kept whole, so the model can be read back and reapplied to new data; the coefficients, hyperparameters and structural parameters that the fit reached; and the record of the run that produced them.

Reach the contents through the accessors rather than the properties where one exists: coef.StatmodFit(), vcov.StatmodFit(), predict.StatmodFit(), summary.StatmodFit(), logLik.StatmodFit().

Usage

StatmodFit(
  spec = NULL,
  coefficients = list(),
  structural = list(),
  hyper = list(),
  loglik = integer(0),
  objective = integer(0),
  edf = NULL,
  fitted = list(),
  converged = logical(0),
  aliased = character(0),
  elapsed = integer(0),
  criterion = integer(0),
  history = list(),
  methods = list(),
  call = NULL,
  bootstrap = new.env(parent = emptyenv())
)

Arguments

spec

The StatmodSpec() that was fitted, with every refreshable term as the fit left it.

coefficients

A named list, one numeric vector per distribution parameter.

structural

A named list with one entry per structural term. Each entry is a list with the term's parameters on their own scale (parameter), on the unconstrained scale (unconstrained), the equation that carries the term (equation) and the names of the parameters that the term holds (held).

hyper

The hyperparameters, keyed by distribution parameter and then by term.

loglik

The weighted log-likelihood at the fitted coefficients, a single number. It is the conditional one.

objective

The penalized objective there, not averaged.

edf

A data frame of effective degrees of freedom with the columns parameter, term, coefficients and edf, one row per term of each equation. The count of a term is its share of \(\mathrm{tr}[(H+S)^{-1}H]\), with \(H\) the information of the log-likelihood and \(S\) the second derivative of the penalty, and it is read at fit time on one information matrix, which methods records as edf_information. That matrix is the information of aic() or bic() where either prices the fit (the count is part of the criterion), otherwise the information of reml() or ml() (distributions7::observed_info() by default), and the information of the inner fit (inner_information of statmod(), with auto_info() settled against the family) only where the model has no outer criterion. For a positive semidefinite \(H\) the total lies in \([0, p]\), with \(p\) the number of coefficients, and the count of a term lies between 0 and its number of coefficients. An indefinite observed information can give a negative share to a direction of negative curvature, and then these bounds can fail. summary.StatmodFit() reports the count on the information of its vcov_type and leaves fit@edf unchanged.

fitted

A named list of the fitted parameters, one vector per distribution parameter.

converged

A single logical. Where the fit does not alternate between blocks, it is the verdict of the inner method. Where the model has a kinked block or a structural term, it is read at the point reached: the Newton decrement of the smooth part and the optimality decrement of every coefficient that a kinked penalty holds at zero are both within mode_error_limit(). A term that recomputes its own block, such as a break-point term, contributes its own verdict in place of that of the inner method.

aliased

The labels, as coef_labels() names them, of the coefficients that the fitted point does not identify. A coefficient is listed when the pivoted decomposition of the inner fit drops it, when the penalized information at the fitted point is singular in its direction (this applies to every decomposition and to an optimizers7 inner optimizer), or when its design column has vanished. The vector is empty where the design has full rank. The estimate, standard error and interval of a listed coefficient are reported as missing, and it is not counted in the degrees of freedom. The stored coefficient keeps the value that it had when the coordinate was left out of the increment, so every predictor reads the vector unchanged.

elapsed

The elapsed time in seconds.

criterion

The value of the criterion that chose the hyperparameters: reml(), ml(), aic(), bic() or cv(), including the criterion that swept the path of a kinked penalty. The value is NA when no criterion ran.

history

A list of data frames recording the run: outer, blocks and inner. An entry is NULL where the run produced no such record.

methods

A list of what was settled during the run, which can differ from what was supplied: smooth, the inner method after iwls() has settled its information (never "auto"); outer, the criterion after resolution, NULL when no marginal or prediction-error criterion ran; search, the optimizer that the outer search used; pinned, the coordinates that the criterion left out of its determinant; kkt, the edge violations that survived the restarts; sparse, the blocks of kinked penalties; sparse_criterion, the criterion that swept their paths; and sparse_hyper, the hyperparameters that it reached.

call

The matched call.

Value

An object of class StatmodFit with one property per argument above.

See also

statmod(), which builds one, summary.StatmodFit() for the printed report, statmod_certificate() for the verdict on convergence.

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(30))
dd$y <- 1 + 2 * dd$x + rnorm(30, sd = 0.3)
fit <- statmod(y ~ x, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)

S7::S7_inherits(fit, StatmodFit)
#> [1] TRUE

# The coefficients form one vector per parameter of the family.
fit@coefficients
#> $mu
#> [1] 1.030728 1.985136
#> 
#> $sigma
#> [1] -1.438298
#> 
fit@converged
#> [1] TRUE
